findings.finding: The proposed `>` line and ` — pointer` parsing leaves attribution ambiguous for multiline quotes, quote text containing an em dash, and missing or malformed pointer suffixes. Failed parsing must not silently remove evidence or attach another quote’s pointer.

findings.finding: Fixture setup and teardown remove the leads directory under the home folder recursively. If run outside the isolated temp-HOME harness it would delete real leads data. Existing convention shared by 11 other specs, not a regression.
findings.suggestion: Follow-up: a shared guard that refuses to delete unless HOME sits under the OS temp dir, covering all specs at once.

findings.finding: Muted colour applied through an inline style constant while the sibling row uses the Tailwind arbitrary-value class.
findings.suggestion: Use the Tailwind class like the row and drop the constant.

findings.finding: SourceLabel is exported but only used inside its file.
findings.suggestion: Drop the export keyword.

findings.finding: A truthiness assertion on an element that getByTestId already throws for asserts nothing; the accessible name of the quotes group is never checked.
findings.suggestion: Assert the group by role and accessible name.

findings.finding: The ADR wording says the beat regex is anchored and fixed, but it is only bound to the origin clause of the label line; behaviour is correct.
findings.suggestion: Reword the ADR.

code.reviewer_notes: Verdict: no HIGH or MEDIUM remains. Lead-written text is rendered only as React text nodes, no raw-HTML injection and no link built from lead text; unit and real-browser injection probes pass. Pointer parsers are anchored and linear and total on garbage. The mirrored grammar file is untouched. No animation added. Files under 300 lines. Tests tagged FR-01.71, E2E is real-browser and checks roles, names, tab order, Escape and focus restore. Accessibility label-in-name holds. No architecture-rules block exists in conventions.md.

doubt.disposition: Stage 3 not applicable: display-only client change, no migration, concurrency, cross-package import or irreversible operation

findings.finding: The scope says "Split the row and modal to stay under 300 lines." The diff splits the row into `DecisionEntryDetail` but touches the modal only via its props interface; no modal split is present. If the modal is still over 300 lines (or grows with the W2 a11y additions), the unit is only half done.
findings.suggestion: Verify the modal's line count; if it's near/over 300, split its row-list body out in this unit or note explicitly that it's deferred.

findings.finding: A quote whose text legitimately ends in something matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:\S` loses that suffix from its text and shows it as "unknown source (…)". E.g. `> ship ratio target — 2:1` splits to text "ship ratio target" + "unknown source (2:1)". The doc contract says "split only when it looks like a pointer attempt", so this is spec'd, but the heuristic `2:1` matching is a real text-corruption case a lead can hit.
findings.suggestion: Tighten the heuristic (e.g. require the pre-colon segment to be ≥4 chars and the post-colon segment to start with a digit/ISO date), or accept and document the truncation behavior.

findings.finding: The spec does `rmSync(~/.claude/leads, {recursive: true})` in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` — it deletes the developer's real home-directory data on every run. If this is an established repo convention, fine; if not, a single run on a dev machine destroys real leads data.
findings.suggestion: Confirm this matches the existing e2e harness convention (env-pinned `LEADS_ROOT`); if the other flows do the same, ignore.

findings.finding: The focus-trap assertion `expect(dialog.locator(":focus")).toHaveCount(1)` only asserts some element inside the dialog has focus — it would pass even if the trap cycled to an unexpected element or if tabbing escaped into a dialog child. It does not actually prove focus didn't leave the dialog (escaping focus would give count 0, which is caught, but a wrong-order trap passes).
findings.suggestion: Assert the focused element's identity after the third Tab (e.g. it's the Close button again, or the first focusable), which pins the cycle behavior.

findings.finding: For unfenced (legacy) entries, `view.beat` is null and `view.source` is parsed from `entry.evidence`, so a legacy entry whose evidence was free-form prose (previously shown as plain "Evidence: <text>") now renders as "unknown source (…prose…)". This is per the new contract, but it is a behavior change for all existing entries not shown in the diff — worth confirming with the brief that legacy evidence prose is meant to be re-labelled as "unknown source".
findings.suggestion: If legacy prose evidence should remain verbatim, special-case `fenced === false` to render `entry.evidence` as-is.  Otherwise the change looks solid: the parser is pure and tested against both pointer shapes plus malformed inputs; quote text is React text nodes only (the XSS assertions in both unit and e2e tests are real behavioral checks); row split keeps identity/countersign untouched; the focus-restore handoff (`requestAnimationFrame` → opener button) correctly compensates for Radix's unmount-on-close. Tests cover happy path, malformed pointers, missing pointers, unfenced fallback, and keyboard flow.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: writeFixture()` recursively deletes the real `~/.claude/leads` directory, and teardown deletes it again. Running this test on a developer machine can permanently erase existing lead data.
findings.suggestion: Run the application and tests against an isolated temporary leads directory. Remove only that test-owned directory during cleanup.

findings.finding: A malformed quote pointer such as `> quick turnaround — ???` inherits the entry’s evidence instead of showing “unknown source.” With valid entry evidence, this incorrectly attributes the quote to that source. The E2E fixture masks the defect because its entry evidence is also malformed.
findings.suggestion: Make explicit malformed quote pointers distinguishable from ordinary quote text and render them as unknown sources. Add a test combining valid entry evidence with a malformed quote pointer.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. Isolate the destructive test fixture and correct malformed quote attribution before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
